title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) testing whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The preregistered contract enforced shared_initial_generation (one initial model output per task reused for both baseline and guarded conditions) to isolate repair-mediated differences from generator sampling variance. We executed 200 paired tasks (50 per prespecified stratum: IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step) with declared generator gpt-5-mini and repair budget ≤1 repair per task. All archived scoring artifacts show both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), yielding paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0, paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair_count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not computable. We explain this degenerate null in light of the preregistration choices, provide concise deterministic validator semantics that define the primary outcome, give execution-accounting diagnostics, and provide reproducible pointers to the archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent-to-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational productivity but raises safety concerns: a single incorrect command can cause outages, violate access control policies, or create routing instability. A common proposed mitigation places a deterministic verifier (sandbox) between generation and deployment in a generate→validate→repair workflow: the verifier flags semantic or policy violations and an automated repair or human gate corrects or blocks unsafe proposals. Prior literature proposes verifier-in-the-loop workflows and layered controls, but controlled quantification of a verifier's marginal benefit—separating repair-mediated corrections from generator sampling variance—remains limited.

We preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 to answer a focused confirmatory question: does integrating a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors compared to LLM-only generation when the initial generation is shared across conditions (shared_initial_generation)? Shared_initial_generation intentionally isolates repair-mediated differences (any paired discordance must arise from repair activity) at the cost of reducing the empirical frequency of initial failures. Our contributions are: (1) a sealed preregistered paired-trial design that enforces shared_initial_generation to attribute effects to repair; (2) a completed, fully archived execution on 200 paired tasks balanced across four prespecified strata with deterministic per-episode validator traces; and (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation of a degenerate null outcome together with concrete reproducible follow-ups that trade off generator variance, repair budget, and validator fidelity.
sections.related_work:
LLM applications to NetOps have grown rapidly: intent-driven configuration synthesis, constrained generation for virtualized network functions, and prototype remediation/repair loops appear in recent conference and preprint work (Nguyen Tu et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2025; NetSoft 2024; ICNP 2025). Generate→validate→repair and bounded self-correction patterns are proposed repeatedly as operational mitigations and appear in prototype agentic workflows (Sang 2025; Okula 2026). Surveys and architecture papers emphasize that operational reliability depends on system design (tool integration, evidence traces, human gates) rather than on model capability alone (Bilal et al., 2026; Malik 2026). Separate lines of work develop failure-mode taxonomies for agentic AI systems and recommend layered defenses and auditability (Maharaj 2026; Vadlamudi 2026).

Our study differs from prior prototypes by (a) preregistering a single primary estimand in a paired design, (b) enforcing shared_initial_generation to attribute any effect specifically to repair activity, and (c) fully archiving deterministic per-episode validator traces and reconciliation artifacts to support reproducible interpretation and exact diagnostics. The experimental design complements earlier proposals that recommend verifier-in-the-loop architectures by providing a sealed, inferentially principled test of repair-mediated marginal benefit under a narrowly constrained contract.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The sealed preregistration (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1; preregistration_sha256: aa4055d52c118741524c4c42d07efa977372be338b9bd96069dc7abfc5b32ac4) specified a paired primary estimand: the absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rates (guarded − baseline). A task is 'validator-clean' when the deterministic validator reports zero violations on the final configuration. Inferential test: exact McNemar two-sided test (α = 0.05). We estimate bootstrap 95% percentile CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) as preregistered.

Sample, strata, and contract enforcement: The confirmatory sample was 200 distinct intent-to-configuration tasks in a paired design (200 tasks × 2 conditions = 400 episodes). Tasks were deterministically generated and balanced across four prespecified strata (50 tasks each): IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step. These strata counts were enforced by the deterministic task generator and are recorded in the authoritative manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b). Inclusion/exclusion rules in the preregistration removed tasks requiring unsupported Batfish scenario features; no exclusions occurred in the final run.

Shared_initial_generation adapter semantics: To attribute differences specifically to repair activity, the preregistered contract produced one initial model generation per task and reused that exact candidate for both the baseline and guarded evaluations (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1). The experimental adapter family (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) implemented a bounded generate→validate→repair transformation with up to one repair attempt per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The declared generator in the archived execution configuration is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider accounting confirms one model call per task under the shared-initial contract (model_calls_used = 200; maximum_model_calls allowed = 400).

Deterministic validator (harm-oracle) semantics: The experiment harness implemented a deterministic Batfish-style verifier; the primary outcome depends on validator-defined violations. For clarity we enumerate the validator failure categories captured in per-episode traces (validator_trace fields): (1) reachability violations — required intra/inter-VLAN or intent-prescribed paths absent after applying the candidate; (2) ACL/policy violations — contradictions with intent-prescribed permit/deny constraints; (3) routing anomalies — detectable loops, next-hop mismatches, or blackholes inconsistent with intent; (4) interface-state and workflow invariant violations — make-before-break, shutdown_configure_restore sequences, group constraints such as one-of-two uplinks must remain up; and (5) dangerous-command flags — commands matched by a regex-based safety detector that mark forbidden operations. Each per-episode validator_trace contains validation_before and validation_after records, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, and a violation_codes list that would contain rule identifiers when violations occur. Representative per-episode scoring traces are archived (for example, execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; sha256: b8ebf9546dabb93b06b15d40152e35a3e96a9d1c98cee131bb7f8065a8b6a2b4) and show violation_count = 0 and repair_applied = false in this run.

Analysis plan, missingness, and sensitivity: Primary analysis used an exact McNemar two-sided test on paired validator-clean/error binary outcomes. Paired absolute difference point estimate and 95% bootstrap percentile CIs (10,000 resamples) were computed with archived seed. The preregistered missingness policy used a complete-pair rule (exclude task pairs with technical failures); a sensitivity analysis treating failed guarded episodes as errors was preregistered but not invoked because there were no technical failures in execution. All analysis code, per-episode validator logs, and reconciliation artifacts are archived and referenced below.
sections.results:
Execution and artifact accounting: Execution completed the full preregistered 400 episodes (200 tasks × 2 conditions) with zero failed episodes (execution started_at_utc = 2026-08-28T11:15:20.528566+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-08-28T11:37:01.389670+00:00). Provider accounting shows model_calls_used = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, and cross-condition cache reuse = false. Representative reproducibility pointers include execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: 9ec4eb2ce01f16d9eb0191b80eda199ec2655637aa2c6c775f8babb62962b46f) and execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b).

Primary paired outcomes and exact counts: Aggregated scoring artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv; sha256: 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951) indicate baseline validator-clean = 200/200 and guarded validator-clean = 200/200. The four-cell paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) is n_11 = 200 (both-clean), n_10 = 0 (guarded-only-clean), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-clean), n_00 = 0 (both-error). The point estimate for paired difference (guarded − baseline) is 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples; archived seed = 1729) yields 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. All numeric outputs are deterministic given the archived artifacts and are available in analysis/results.json (input_results_sha256: 9ec4eb2c... in the bundle).

Repair activity and secondary estimand: Because no validator-detected errors occurred for any shared initial candidate, the bounded repair policy was never invoked (repair_count = 0). Per-episode guarded traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; sha256: 020baed3e0e4283cc5e25413af002166998bfc587a1919046ca53dab09251b30) confirm repair_applied = false and repair_prompt_sha256 = null. Consequently, the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate — the fraction of initial-error tasks where final config is validator-clean) is not empirically computable from these data.

Diagnostics, contamination, and reconciliation: Automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty. Missingness artifacts show complete_pairs = 200 and zero missing episodes across conditions (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; sha256: 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c). Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and that all deterministic checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). These artifacts substantiate that the observed null result is not due to execution loss or manifest mismatches.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the degenerate null: Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract and the supplied synthetic 200-task corpus, the declared generator produced validator-clean candidates for every task; validation_after.violation_count = 0 across episodes. Given that design, a bounded repair loop constrained to act only if the validator flags a violation will never be exercised. Thus the observed paired difference of 0.0 is a deterministic consequence of the contract and the specific generator+task-bank pairing: it provides evidence for the conditional statement "given a generator that produces validator-clean shared candidates under this synthetic task bank, a bounded validator/repair wrapper produces no measurable paired improvement." The experiment does not answer whether a repair loop would help when independent generation produces unsafe candidates, when repair budgets are larger, or when validator semantics differ.

Design trade-offs and operational implications: Shared_initial_generation improves causal attribution—any discordance must derive from repair—but it reduces the probability of observing baseline failures and therefore reduces the chance to measure repair efficacy. Practitioners should treat shared vs independent generation as answering distinct operational questions: shared_initial_generation isolates repair effectiveness conditional on a fixed candidate; independent generation evaluates end-to-end risk reduction when generation is stochastic. The archived bundle allows reproducible follow-ups to cross this axis: (A) switch to independent condition generation (two independent model calls per task) to increase baseline failure probability and enable repair opportunities; (B) increase the repair budget or enable iterative repair/tool-assisted repair to measure repair throughput; (C) enrich the validator harm-oracle with vendor-specific quirks or extended telemetry to increase sensitivity to subtle semantic regressions. Each suggested follow-up reuses the canonical task manifest and scoring harness in the bundle.

Threats to validity and scope: Construct validity depends on whether the deterministic Batfish-style validator models the operational harms of interest. Our validator encodes explicit workflow invariants, reachability, ACL/policy checks, routing anomaly detection, and a dangerous-command detector; however, it does not emulate every vendor nuance or production telemetry. External validity is constrained by: a single declared generator family (gpt-5-mini), a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair), and a synthetic task corpus. Consequently, conclusions do not generalize across all models, repair strategies, or production environments. Finally, adversarial prompt-injection and red-team scenarios were not included and remain important future directions.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed preregistered paired trial to measure the marginal effect of a deterministic Batfish-style validator in a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline under a shared_initial_generation contract. For the synthetic 200-task bank and declared generator (gpt-5-mini) used here, every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: both baseline and guarded arms were validator-clean on all tasks, yielding an exact paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked, so repair efficacy was not observed. These artifact-grounded results do not refute the potential value of verifier-assisted workflows; rather they demonstrate that preregistered contract choices (shared vs independent generation), task-bank challenge level, validator fidelity, and repair policy jointly determine whether verifier assistance yields an observable benefit. The archived execution bundle contains the task manifest, raw responses, per-episode validator traces, paired contingency tables, and reconciliation logs necessary to reproduce the run and to design follow-ups that trade off generator variance and repair opportunity to quantify repair-mediated gains in realistic settings.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-style sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single declared model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

The preregistered shared_initial_generation contract produced exactly one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduced the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
